_comment: The detector-residual ratchet for this surface: the statically-erased or renamed forms DELIBERATELY outside the corpus contract, per rule — known limits of precise, low-false-positive detection, recorded as data so a rule's page states where its detection ends instead of leaving it to guesswork. The list only shrinks: closing a residual means seeding the corpus case that contracts it and deleting the entry here, never silently. Every key is a catalog rule id of this surface, and the keys are sorted; held by tests/architecture/test_rule_standard.py.

backend/errors_use_the_typed_envelope: an error constructed under an alias (`from fastapi import HTTPException as ApiError`) is not required to be resolved back to the framework's HTTP error
backend/expand_revisions_only_expand: an operation made in a helper function that `upgrade()` calls, or through an alias of the operations handle under a method name no operation has, is not required to be seen: the reference stack's migration run refuses it as it executes, which is the half of the rule that sees every operation

the order of operations inside one revision is not required to be followed: an operation on a table, or over a column, that the same revision creates or adds is admitted wherever it sits in `upgrade()`, while the run admits it only after the creation
backend/module_list_is_unconditional: a module list built in another file than the one that calls `create_app` (imported as a name, or returned by an imported function) is not required to be followed: the rule reads one file at a time

a module object that is itself `None` under a condition (`oidc_module = build(...) if ISSUER else None` in another file) and is then named unconditionally is not required to be seen: `create_app` refuses a list entry that is no module, so the form fails at composition where the condition does not hold
a list chosen by a boolean operator (`modules or defaults`) or by an index into a table of lists is not required to be seen
backend/no_destructive_migrations: a statement the source does not spell out (a variable, a value a helper returns, a query-builder construct such as `op.execute(notes.delete())`, a file read at run time) is not required to be read: only a statement written as a literal, an f-string or a concatenation of strings is

an operation whose name is computed (`getattr(op, name)(...)` with a name that is not a literal, source text run through `exec`) is not required to be read: an operation is read under its own name, under a name the revision imports it as at its top level, or through `getattr` with a literal name

a step the upgrade reaches other than by calling a top-level function of the same revision by its name (a helper imported from another module, a callable held in a variable, a method, a function passed as a value and called through it) is not required to be followed
an upgrade entry point bound to anything but a top-level function of the revision, directly or through a chain of top-level names (`upgrade = make_upgrade()`), is not required to be resolved
rows deleted through an object-relational session rather than by a statement or a schema operation (`session.delete(row)`, `session.query(Note).delete()`) are not required to be read as a drop
a revision file in a subdirectory of the versions directory, which the migration tool loads only when it is configured to search recursively, is not required to be read

a unique, foreign-key or unique-index constraint on a column the same upgrade adds nullable is not required to be reported when that upgrade fills the column before adding the constraint, which is the one order in which the existing rows can break it
a constraint written inline in a raw column addition (`ADD COLUMN slug text UNIQUE DEFAULT 'x'`, `ADD COLUMN rank int NOT NULL`) is not required to be read as a step the existing rows can break
backend/no_dynamic_sql: SQL built as a string and handed to a raw DB-API cursor (`cursor.execute(f"SELECT ... FROM {table}")`) is not required to be caught: the check matches the reference stack's `text(...)` construct, and a package that does not model the schema it talks to never writes one. The shape is not ungoverned — the reference stack delegates it to a stock analyzer's SQL-string-construction rule, in the platform repository and in every generated project as a blocking step — but that lane is outside the catalog, so the limit is recorded here rather than implied
an alias-renamed symbol import (`from sqlalchemy import text as sql_text`) is not required to be resolved to `text`
backend/no_exception_text_in_responses: an error built into a local name and raised on a later statement (`err = ValidationFailedError(str(exc))` then `raise err`) is not required to be connected to the handler that bound the exception
a helper called from the handler that takes the caught exception and returns a message string is not required to be followed across the call

exception text a handler persists instead of raising (`row.failure_reason = str(exc)`, on a column a read DTO later exposes) is not required to be followed to the response that eventually serves it: a write and a subsequent request separate the two, so no static check connects them
backend/no_framework_patching: a name bound to the framework in another file (`from app.wiring import kernel`, where `kernel` is `terp.core.app`) is not required to be followed: the rule reads one file at a time, and follows a name only through plain assignments
a reference reached through a call (`getattr(terp.core, 'app').create_app = ...`, a function that returns the module) is not required to be seen
a module replaced in `sys.modules` under a key that is not a string literal is not required to be seen
a file under a `tests` directory is not read, so a replacement made there and imported by app code is not required to be seen
a change to what the framework reads instead of to its functions (`os.environ['ENVIRONMENT'] = 'local'` before the settings are read, `os.chdir` before the app is composed) is not this rule's subject
a function changed without an assignment the source shows (through `ctypes`, or through the garbage collector's references) is not required to be seen
backend/no_manual_actor_stamping: a stamp written through the attribute API (`setattr(row, "created_by_id", ...)`) is not required to be seen as an assignment
a comparison expressed as a method call on the column (`.in_(...)`, `.is_(...)`) rather than as an operator is not required to be seen as a comparison
backend/no_manual_lease_columns: a holder/heartbeat pair under other column names (`worker_id` + `last_seen_at`) is not required to be recognised as a hand-rolled lease: the check matches a fixed set of column spellings on a table model, not the custody shape
backend/no_manual_ownership_checks: a ModuleSpec that omits `services=` is not required to be caught by the composition-time twin, which iterates the declared services
backend/no_raw_outbound_http: dynamic import (`importlib.import_module("httpx")`) is not required to be seen as an import
backend/personal_fields_are_declared: a model whose base comes from another package under a name that is not one of the known model bases (a third-party base model) is not required to be recognised as a model, because the check resolves bases by name within the scanned tree
a model built at runtime (create_model, a class assembled by a factory) is not required to be read: its fields exist only once the code runs
backend/request_timestamps_carry_their_o: an alias of the escape bound in one module and imported into another under a different name counts once, where it is bound, not at each use in the other module
a name reached through a computed attribute (getattr with a name that is not a literal, or an import made by importlib) is not resolved to the escape
a name bound to the escape by a for loop, a with statement or an assignment expression counts where the escape is named, not at each use of that name
the boundary's own module reached through a package's namespace (`vars(terp.core)` or its `__dict__`), or by a module name that is not a literal, is not resolved to that module

the escape's own validator taken out of a schema that declares the escape, and declared on another field by hand, is not resolved to the escape: the rule sees the escape where it is named, and only there
an early validator on a timestamp field is not resolved where the field, or the validator, belongs to a base from another module, because the check resolves a base by its name within the file
a timestamp alias imported from another module (from app.types import Stamp) is not resolved to a timestamp, so an early validator on it, or on a field typed with it, is not counted

a validator of the whole model (model_validator in before or wrap mode, Pydantic 1's root_validator with pre=True) is not counted: it sees the body rather than a field, so counting it would mostly be noise (ADR 0206, Open)

a validator a schema gets only at run time is not resolved: create_model's __validators__, validators unpacked into the metadata (Annotated[datetime, *EARLY]), returned by a function of the app's own, or built with GetPydanticSchema, and a type whose own __get_pydantic_core_schema__ reads the text

a LocalTimeIn that names a place keeping UTC all year (Africa/Abidjan, Atlantic/Reykjavik) reads text without an offset as UTC, as the escape does, and is not counted as the escape: it names a place, which is what a reviewer reads, and reads that place's wall time correctly (ADR 0207, a known limit the owner accepted)
